To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) people do not have the knowledge required for making rational market-style choices in the health sector, (2) people's knowledge is related to their socio-economic status and (3) the health information provided by the media and by health care professionals does not meet the needs of consumers.
the British public is not well informed about health matters and that, in consequence, the market model of general medical practice cannot work.

the majority of British people do not know the location or telephone number of their general practice and do not know how many doctors work in it, but that the majority of them do know how to contact their doctor in an emergency.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of whether the market model is appropriate for primary health care.
the extent of consumer knowledge about general practice.
the question of whether or not patients have sufficient information to make the market-style choices implied by the new model for the provision of primary care.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the market model of health care reform is not viable unless the public are given more knowledge and information about health care.
the British public is not yet ready for market-style health care reform.
the British consumer lacks sufficient information about general practitioners' services and the health care system to make informed choices about which general practitioner to consult.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the NHS is in a state of flux, and it is not clear whether the new market model will be successful or not.
the British public has very limited knowledge of the health services available to it, and that the information it does possess is of poor quality.
the British public lacks the information needed to choose a GP.

policy makers should be wary of assuming that patients have the knowledge required to make informed choices about their health care.   1.
